::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** October 10, 1890.  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Coleridge, <i>[Life](other_books/otherbook_40.qmd)</i> 321
:::

My dear[Florence](people/person_1520.qmd)
I am very glad to hear of you again, and I hope the touch of frost will not be felt at Bournemouth;  it has spared all our flowers as yet.  I waited to write because [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd) was coming to make up our plans for the new [volume](organizations/other_52.qmd).  We will try to put in 'Purification' poem for February, but I am afraid poems do not get much payment.  I wish I could put more work in [her](people/person_1519.qmd) way. [^1]  I forget whether you know [Miss Hill](people/person_2102.qmd), who stays with the [Jones Bateman](people/person_785.qmd)s sometimes;  she is lame from old hip complaint, but gets about on her crutches.  She is sister to Mr. Rowland Hill.  I am afraid the [*Newbery Magazine*](organizations/other_83.qmd) is a tardy affair, as all magazines are, unless they begin by being hard-hearted and summary.  I don't much like what I have seen of it.  Christabel asks to be remembered to you.  She is my original old [Gosling](organizations/other_104.qmd), and she and I have been going over our old brood, and what a remarkable set they have been, for good, and alas! sometimes for the reverse, but there are a good many that I am proud of.[^2]

I am hurried and must finish.

Your affectionate
C. M. Yonge

---

[^1]: Her correspondent’s sister Emma Wilford (b. 1832/3), as appears from the next letter to Florence Wilford (18 October 1890).  They lived together in Bournemouth.  A poem ‘The Treasures of the Snow: Feast of the Purification’, signed ‘W.’ appeared in *MP* (February 1891).  The feast of the Purification is 2 February, and this may well be Emma Wilford’s poem.
[^2]: The Goslings who had been remarkable for the reverse were probably [Mary Arnold](people/person_1467.qmd) and [Mildred Coleridge](people/person_17.qmd).  The former had, as Mrs Humphry Ward, become the author of the notorious novel *Robert Elsmere* (1888), about an Anglican clergyman's loss of faith;  the latter, who was a cousin of CMY's, fell in love with the unsuitable Charles Warren Adams, and after a series of acrimonious libel suits brought by him against her father and brother, married him in 1885 in a blaze of publicity, causing a family quarrel which was never made up.     Another backslider was probably [Katie Johns](people/person_887.qmd), who seems to have parted from her husband and become a theosophist.
